name: Bowline
description: Forms a fixed loop at the end of a rope. Essential for mooring and rescue operations.

steps.instruction: Form a small loop near the end of the rope, leaving a long working end (the 'tail').
Pass the tail up through the loop from underneath.
Wrap the tail around the standing part of the rope (behind the loop).
Pass the tail back down through the loop from the top.
Tighten by pulling the standing part and the loop in opposite directions.

name: Clove Hitch
description: Quick attachment knot for securing a rope to a post, spar, or ring.

steps.instruction: Wrap the rope around the post once, crossing over the standing part.
Wrap around the post a second time, crossing above the first wrap.
Pass the tail under the second wrap and pull tight.
Add a half hitch with the tail for extra security if the load is variable.

name: Reef Knot (Square Knot)
description: Joins two ropes of equal diameter. Used for reefing sails and securing bundles.

steps.instruction: Hold one rope in each hand. Cross the right over the left and tie a half knot.
Cross the left over the right and tie a second half knot.
Ensure both parts exit on the same side — both standing parts on top, both tails on bottom.
Pull all four ends simultaneously to tighten evenly.

name: Round Turn and Two Half Hitches
description: Reliable mooring knot that maintains tension under load.

steps.instruction: Pass the rope twice around the bollard or ring (round turn).
Pass the tail over the standing part to form a half hitch.
Form a second half hitch below the first, in the same direction.
Pull the standing part to take up slack, then tighten both hitches.

name: Figure-Eight Knot
description: Stopper knot that prevents a rope from running through a block or fairlead.

steps.instruction: Form a loop by crossing the tail over the standing part.
Pass the tail under the standing part and up through the loop.
The finished knot should resemble the numeral 8.
Dress the knot by tightening each turn evenly.
